question: Which landmark event in 1846 is credited with ushering in the era of modern anaesthesia?

answers.text: James Young Simpson introduced chloroform anaesthesia in Edinburgh

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Simpson introduced chloroform in 1847, one year after Morton's ether demonstration — an important milestone but not the first public demonstration of surgical anaesthesia.

answers.text: William Morton publicly demonstrated ether anaesthesia at Massachusetts General Hospital

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! On 16 October 1846, Morton demonstrated ether anaesthesia in the Ether Dome at Massachusetts General Hospital, transforming surgery from a brutal ordeal to a controlled procedure.

answers.text: Crawford Long used ether for minor surgery in Georgia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Long used ether in 1842 privately but did not publish his findings until 1849, so his work was not publicly recognised as the founding event of anaesthesia.

answers.text: Humphry Davy described the analgesic properties of nitrous oxide

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Davy described nitrous oxide's properties around 1800, but this remained theoretical — it was Morton's public surgical demonstration in 1846 that catalysed modern anaesthesia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the timeline of anaesthesia history. Morton's public demonstration of ether at Massachusetts General Hospital on 16 October 1846 is universally recognised as the birth of modern anaesthesia.
Well done! Morton's 1846 ether demonstration at the Ether Dome is the defining founding event of anaesthesiology as a specialty.
